title: Klopp leads backlash as Infantino faces calls to resign
snippet: Former Liverpool manager, politicians and football bodies angry after Trump admits lobbying Fifa president to suspend US player's ban.

James Ducker Published 07 July 2026 1:11pm BST Jürgen Klopp led a furious backlash against Gianni Infantino, who faces calls to resign after Fifa overturned US striker Folarin Balogun’s World Cup suspension.Infantino, the Fifa president and most powerful figure in football, was engulfed by crisis on Monday after Donald Trump admitted lobbying him to overturn Balogun’s dismissal against Bosnia and Herzegovina.The decision meant the striker was allowed to play in the last-16 tie against Belgium on Monday night and Balogun was named in the United States’s starting XI, paving the way for the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) to potentially pursue legal action.The RBFA informed the US Soccer Federation before the game that it “contests the eligibility” of Balogun “should the player be listed on the referee’s team sheet” and that this would leave “all further actions open”.Infantino was spared a nightmare scenario as the US self-destructed against Belgium to crash out of the World Cup. Two goals from Charles De Ketelaere, before an atrocious error from US goalkeeper Matt Freese helped to gift Hans Vanaken a goal, contributed to a 4-1 thrashing for the co-hosts and averted a fresh explosion in the Balogun controversy. Romelu Lukaku scored the fourth. Folarin Balogun failed to make the most of his reprieve, drawing a blank as the US were eliminated Credit: Christopher Torres/Shutterstock In a press conference in the Oval Office on Monday, the US president said he asked for a “review” of Balogun’s sending-off, because he “didn’t think it was a foul”.Fifa’s scrapping of Balogun’s suspension after Trump’s intervention has provoked the first major rebellion in the game against Infantino.Klopp, the former Liverpool manager, Uefa and the federations of Germany and Belgium launched unprecedented attacks on Infantino, who has faced repeated accusations of cosying up to Trump. Jurgen Klopp has been critical of Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino Credit: Hannah McKay/Reuters “This is our sport, not theirs,” Klopp said. “If Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino really sorted this out between themselves, it is madness; it calls everything into question.”Calls for Infantino to resign then followed from senior MPs, campaigners and David Bernstein, the former Football Association chairman.Bernstein, who had been a leading voice in challenging Infantino’s disgraced predecessor Sepp Blatter, said the Balogun situation was “absolutely wrong, awful”.“It hits at one of the beauties of football – the worldwide application across the world of regulations and rules,” he said as politicians from all parties moved to condemn Infantino.Fifa invoked a little-known article in its rules to “suspend” for one year the red card Balogun received in the US’s 2-0 win against Bosnia and Herzegovina in San Francisco on Wednesday. Balogun (centre) was controversially sent off against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before earning a reprieve Credit: Martin Meissner/AP Fifa’s decision to rescind Balogun’s ban has opened up a can of worms and the Football Association is weighing up whether to challenge Jarell Quansah’s suspension after he was sent off in England’s 3-2 win against Mexico. France are now also attempting to have Michael Olise’s yellow card in their victory over Paraguay annulled.Sources close to talks claim Trump discussed the matter three times with Infantino.Infantino maintains Fifa’s decision on Balogun was independent, and unrelated to his conversation with the US president. Gianni Infantino’s close relationship with Donald Trump has attracted widespread criticism Credit: AFP via Getty Images But Trump had already claimed credit for getting the red card overturned. “I’m the one that got them to do it,” Trump said.“I saw the play, and I’m a person that loves sports.
